items.title: UV Fluorescence Sensing of Medical-Chemical-and- Biological Analytes by an AlGaN/Si-on-Sapphire Optoelectronic Chip
items.summary: arXiv:2610.13525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes and analyzes a compact fluorescence-photometer lab-on-a-chip that is simpler than a fluorescence spectrometer, and that does not require spectrum reconstruction by a computer. An on-chip AlGaN VCSEL lasing at 280 nm, or at 310 nm, pumps an on-chip sample in the form of liquid or solid or tissue, thereby exciting signature fluorescence in the 300 to 540 nm wavelength range. This emission signal is detected and read out by an on-chip UV-enhanced Silicon photodiode. The 2 cm x 5 cm chip consists of C-plane (0001) Sapphire, and no lenses, prisms, or mirrors are utilized in the photometer. The chip is opto-electronic and features co-packaged electronics using tiny electronic chiplets that are bonded to the sapphire. These consist of an LD driver and transimpedance amplifier for the UV photonics, together with ASICs, ADC, microcontroller, micro-battery and RF-wireless or Ethernet chiplets. The mission of this self-contained cost-effective chip is sensing targeted medical-chemical-biological (MCB) agents in a local or network setting. Eight significant MCB applications are detailed here.

items.title: Aubry-Andr\'e transition in photonic time quasicrystals
items.summary: arXiv:2610.13538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In one dimension, Anderson localization by a disordered potential sets in at any strength, whereas localization by a quasiperiodic potential in the Aubry-Andr\'e model occurs through a transition at a critical strength. Disordered photonic time crystals exhibit a temporal counterpart of this Anderson localization, in which light, instead of decaying in space, stops propagating and grows in time. Whether a counterpart of the Aubry-Andr\'e transition exists in photonic time quasicrystals remains an open question. Here we show that it does, and that the transition occurs at mobility edges in momentum rather than in energy. These edges arise even under impulsive modulation, where the field obeys the self-dual almost-Mathieu equation exactly, and for general analytic modulations Avila's global theory reveals the condition under which they form. The Aubry-Andr\'e transition thus extends from spatial lattices to the time domain, where it sorts light by wave number into components that propagate and components that stop and grow.

items.title: Topologically steerable ultra-flat electro-optic combs via non-Hermitian frequency lattices
items.summary: arXiv:2610.12867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electro-optic (EO) frequency combs convert microwave signals to the optical domain with deterministic repetition rates, enabling applications in optical telecommunications, microwave photonics, and LiDAR. However, generating flat EO combs has remained a long-standing challenge due to exponential decay of the spectral envelope inherent to bidirectional frequency coupling within conventional schemes. Here we reveal the inherent correspondence between flat-comb generation and the topological energy bands of non-Hermitian nonreciprocal frequency lattices, and experimentally realize ultra-flat combs with topologically controlled spectral flow. We derive the exact analytical condition for flat-comb generation, and find that it maps precisely onto the complex energy band, thereby establishing a direct connection between comb-envelope engineering and non-Hermitian topology. Experimentally, we observe an ultra-flat comb whose frequency evolution direction is governed by the topological winding and remains robust against detuning and phase fluctuations. This scheme can be further extended to long-range coupling and multi-lattice architectures, underscoring its versatility for flat dual- and multi-comb generation. Our work establishes a topologically steerable approach for achieving ultra-flat EO combs, paving the way for chip-scale spectral engineering via non-Hermitian topology.

items.title: Localization Landscapes based on the Green's Matrix of Non-Hermitian Optical Scattering Systems
items.summary: arXiv:2610.13413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Filoche--Mayboroda (FM) localization landscape predicts where the spatially localized modes of a self-adjoint elliptic operator reside without diagonalizing it, but the construction fails for the complex, non-normal Green's matrix G of an open scattering array of electric dipoles. We propose three real-valued, positive landscapes built from the Feinberg--Zee hermitization of G: a regularised Gramian inverse (Gram), the diagonal Schur block that carries the Metz--Neri--Rogers spectral density (SY), and the full hermitized inverse contracted against a polarization-isotropic source pair (Herm). The three form a progression from spectrum-blind to fully hermitisation-faithful, agree in the limit $z\to 0$, and diverge where it matters: at nonzero spectral shift SY resolves modes that Gram collapses, and Herm resolves modes that SY collapses. We demonstrate the progression on random and deterministic aperiodic scattering arrays with a wide range of structural correlations, extend to the vectorial case of transverse electric polarization (TE), and provide rigorous justifications along with mathematical proofs and a complete numerical recipe in the appendices and in the supplementary material.

items.title: Broadband soliton microcombs in the biological window enabled by a resonant coupler
items.summary: arXiv:2610.12603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Broadband soliton microcombs near 1 $\mu$m offer coherent, evenly spaced optical lines for measurements in the biological window. However, combining broad spectral coverage with closely spaced comb lines increases the pump-power requirement and makes thermally stable soliton access more difficult. Here, we demonstrate broadband silicon nitride (Si3N4) soliton microcombs enabled by a resonant coupler that enhances pump delivery to the nonlinear resonator. The device generates a spectrum spanning 930-1380 nm with an approximately 98-GHz comb-line spacing at on-chip pump powers of tens of milliwatts, while providing reliable thermally stable access to the single-soliton state. These results provide a route to compact, power-efficient microcomb sources that combine broad spectral coverage with closely spaced comb lines for spectroscopy and imaging in the biological window.

items.title: Coherent ultraviolet frequency combs generated by resonant dispersive waves
items.summary: arXiv:2610.12620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resonant dispersive wave (RDW) emission in gas-filled anti-resonant hollow-core fibers (AR-HCF) offers a wavelength-tunable route to ultraviolet (UV) and vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) frequency comb generation. RDW emission is expected to be coherent fundamentally, but various noise sources are expected to limit the coherence, including amplitude-to-phase fluctuations due to input pulse intensity noise and plasma formation. It is critical, therefore, to establish the limits of the coherence of UV RDW pulses to determine their applicability for precision spectroscopy. Here, we demonstrate the coherence of RDW emission at 260~nm generated with an amplified Yb-doped fiber system at a 2-MHz repetition rate with a self-heterodyne beat measurement between the RDW and the fourth harmonic of the source. We isolate the RDW contribution to the frequency noise by coherently subtracting the carrier-envelope offset noise contribution measured simultaneously with an f-2f interferometer. We observe a beatnote linewidth below 10~kHz over timescales longer than 100~ms, and we find a conservative upper bound of 1~rad on the integrated RMS phase deviations over a frequency range spanning 1 to 30~kHz. The dominant frequency noise contributions are consistent with environmental noise of the interferometers and AR-HCF coupling fluctuations. These results provide strong evidence that RDW emission is coherent under well-controlled experimental conditions, confirming its potential for UV and VUV frequency comb generation.

items.title: Theory of Disorder-Induced Multimode Coupling in a Fabry-P\'erot Cavity
items.summary: arXiv:2610.12687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strong light--matter interactions have attracted significant interest in physical chemistry due to the potential for modifying molecular processes by hybridizing with cavity photons and forming polaritonic states. However, for a disordered molecular ensemble within an optical cavity capable of supporting multiple photon modes, theoretical understanding of multimode polaritons remains incomplete, particularly regarding whether and how distinct photon modes are mutually coupled through molecules. In this work, we generalize the collective mode expansion formalism to incorporate multiple photonic modes and show that spatial and orientational disorder in the light--matter coupling strength (originating from dipole orientation fluctuations and photonic field inhomogeneity) can mediate cross-mode coupling. This disorder-induced coupling allows for energy transfer to otherwise unexcited photon modes through a mechanism termed disorder-induced multimode activation (DIMA). Using an effective one-dimensional Fabry--P\'erot cavity as a test system, we demonstrate that the cross-mode energy transfer through DIMA can be controlled by changing the molecular layer thickness and the optical properties of the mirrors. Furthermore, we show that DIMA is robust against weak energetic disorder. This mechanistic understanding lays the foundation for a systematic control of multimode photon coupling using disorder-induced effects.

items.title: Phantom Zernike Wavefront Sensor: Phase Contrast with Engineered Focal Plane Reference Speckles
items.summary: arXiv:2610.12807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the Phantom Zernike Wavefront Sensor (phantom ZWFS), an engineered reference extension of phase-contrast wavefront sensing in which controlled pupil plane modulation generates off-axis coherent speckle structures that undergo localized focal plane phase shifts. These references may replace the central ZWFS reference when the on-axis PSF core is required for another optical function, such as photonic science coupling, or may augment a conventional central ZWFS response to provide additional wavefront information. Using a monochromatic scalar model, we derive the resulting carrier structure and show how the engineered references can be recovered through spatial demodulation and incorporated into calibrated reconstruction. A simple four-reference realization demonstrates that the reference geometry redistributes photon sensitivity across spatial frequency magnitude and orientation, producing mode dependent changes in linearity and cross-talk rather than a uniform improvement over a classical ZWFS. We then consider differential piston on a seven segment aperture as an application specific example. A hybrid sensor retaining the central ZWFS phase region and adding six engineered references that match the segment geometry gives similar precision near the phased state but substantially improved performance at larger piston excursions. Under the adopted photon-noise-limited benchmark, the hybrid reduces the nonlinear reconstruction error and provides better conditioned optical encoding of the piston state than an idealized vector ZWFS, allowing more precise piston estimation from the same detected photon flux at larger piston excursions.

items.title: Silent breakdown of the perturbative polarization expansion in the terahertz regime
items.summary: arXiv:2610.12982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear optics expands the polarization in powers of the drive and retains only the lowest-order terms. This truncation is safe at optical frequencies, where the convergence field lies far above the damage threshold. In the terahertz regime, phonon polaritons enhance the nonlinear susceptibilities by orders of magnitude, lowering the convergence field into the sub-damage range and opening a window in which the expansion fails while the crystal remains recoverable. We term this window silent breakdown. At resonance, the nearest singularities of the driven lattice mode are a complex-conjugate pair of branch points below the multistability threshold, so the response remains smooth and single-valued even though the $\chi^{\left( n \right)}$ description fails. The convergence field scales as $Q^{-3/2}$, so sharpening a resonance enhances the nonlinearity but narrows the range over which the expansion applies. It follows from the mode shift $S$ alone, $E_{\mathrm{conv}}=E_{\mathrm{ref}}(3\sqrt{3}QS)^{-1/2}$, giving 2$\sim$9 MV/cm for $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{3}$. Since resonant enhancement is central to terahertz nonlinear optics, this boundary defines the field range over which susceptibility-based descriptions are quantitatively reliable.

items.title: Matrix-free numerical continuation of the Ikeda map in passive Kerr resonators
items.summary: arXiv:2610.12994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a matrix-free numerical continuation framework for the Ikeda map of coherently driven passive Kerr resonators. The framework traces solution branches and evaluates their linear stability without explicitly assembling the full Jacobian matrices, using a unified formulation for states that recur after one or multiple round trips. We resolve stable and unstable branches of modulation-instability patterns and temporal cavity solitons, and uncover period-doubled homogeneous states and associated multi-round-trip dynamics that are absent from the standard Lugiato-Lefever equation (LLE). For period-1 states, the Ikeda map and the LLE show close agreement in the high-finesse regime, while their branch-existence intervals increasingly deviate as the finesse decreases. These results demonstrate that direct continuation of the unaveraged round-trip map can capture nonlinear states and multi-round-trip dynamics beyond the mean-field description, providing a systematic framework for bifurcation and stability analysis of Kerr resonators without relying on the averaged LLE.

items.title: Bottom-Up Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering for the Detection of Micro-Objects and Globular Analytes
items.summary: arXiv:2610.13381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is typically achieved by depositing the analyte on a metal or semiconductor substrate. We propose a bottom-up approach, enabling SERS by depositing a metal on the surface of the object being studied. A Mie-theory analysis of electric-field enhancement in dielectric core-shell particles is presented. A correlative approach combining SERS, atomic force microscopy, and scanning electron microscopy is employed to model the conditions required for sensitive SERS detection and spectral analysis of polystyrene microspheres (PMSs) as models of globular and vesicle-like objects. Based on these findings, we propose a SERS-active system that provides strong signal enhancement (up to four orders of magnitude for a single globular object) while maintaining spectral fidelity, where PMSs act both as model analytes and as integral components of a metal-dielectric resonator.

items.title: Spectral-control-assisted Kerr-lens mode-locking in a Tm:Y2O3 ceramic laser
items.summary: arXiv:2610.13427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report a soft-aperture Kerr-lens mode-locked Tm:Y2O3 ceramic laser stabilized by suppressing wavelength competition under high population-inversion conditions. The laser delivers an average output power of 0.5 W with a pulse duration of 112 fs at a repetition rate of 90 MHz and a central wavelength of 2.08 um. Further optimization for shorter pulses yields a pulse duration of 107 fs, through with a reduced output power of 0.22 W. These results demonstrate that spectral-control is an effective approach for achieving stable mode-locking in such laser with strong spectral competition.

items.title: Chiroptical Nonlinearity Found in Covalent Organic Frameworks
items.summary: arXiv:2610.13728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiroptical nonlinearity is vital for modern optics and photonics. However, it remains a central challenge to obtain a material simultaneously with large second-order nonlinearity and strong nonlinear optical chirality. Here we uncover the strong chiroptical nonlinearity in COF-330-a, owing to the formation of unique chiral, polar structure with large p-electron conjugation via structural transformation. A large effective second-order nonlinear susceptibility of ~ 101 pm/V and a strong nonlinear chiroptical response (SHG-CD: -1.60 to +1.66) have been demonstrated in individual COF-330-a microcrystals, transcending the performance trade-off limitation in conventional chiroptical materials. These findings open a new avenue for designing nonlinear chiroptical crystals which harness the duality of polarity and chirality and chemical versatility of COFs.

items.title: PhySeqNet: physics-informed fluorescent foci detection for BARseq spatial transcriptomics
items.summary: arXiv:2610.13779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: BARseq enables spatially resolved gene-expression profiling across intact tissue, but its sensitivity depends on accurate detection and decoding of dense fluorescent rolonies. Existing spot-calling approaches can be conservative where signals overlap, while supervised deep learning is limited by the lack of reliable manual ground truth in real tissue images. Here we present PhySeqNet, a physics-informed deep learning framework for annotation-free fluorescent foci detection in BARseq. PhySeqNet trains U-Net detectors entirely on semi-synthetic images generated from an instrument-matched optical model combined with real sample-free experimental noise, and is integrated into pyBARseq, a modular Python pipeline for BARseq analysis. PhySeqNet achieved high detection performance on held-out simulated data across wavelength bands. On real tissue images, where ground truth is unavailable, we evaluated detections by forward-model reconstruction: PhySeqNet with conservative barcode-aware non-maxima suppression (NMSB) achieved higher reconstruction fidelity (NCC and MS-SSIM) than the BarDensr single-shot estimator, tuned classical spot detectors, and a pretrained deep-learning detector. In the analyzed brain section, PhySeqNet with NMSB yielded a median of 51 counts per cell versus 47 for BarDensr, with a similar number of genes detected per cell. The recovered transcripts produced spatial expression patterns qualitatively consistent with Allen MERFISH reference data and preserved cell-type composition after scANVI label transfer. These results show that physics-informed simulation can train practical, annotation-free detectors that improve BARseq sensitivity without disrupting downstream biological interpretation.

items.title: Statistical Optical Replication and Mixing of Spatial Information across Wavelengths
items.summary: arXiv:2610.13861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accessing and combining the spatial information carried by light at different wavelengths is important for linking structured-light encoding with spectrally distinct detection channels. Here, we introduce a correlation-enabled linear-optical framework for cross-wavelength imaging, bidirectional replication, and spatial information mixing. Shared random holographic modulation establishes correlations between nondegenerate optical fields, allowing spatial information to be retrieved from joint intensity fluctuations. In the demonstrated replicator, a spatial pattern encoded at one wavelength is read out in the detection coordinates of another through intensity correlations. Selecting diffraction-order pairs produces correlation kernels containing either the product or the conjugate product of two input field envelopes. These operations reproduce the spatial algebra underlying sum- and difference-frequency generation, while the optical fields retain their original carrier frequencies. The theory accounts for wavelength-dependent propagation and coordinate scaling, linking the input structures to observable correlation patterns. Together, these results establish a common framework for cross-wavelength spatial information processing through engineered optical correlations and joint detection.

items.title: Optimal linear-optical interferometers for unitary t-designs in a multi-photon Fock space
items.summary: arXiv:2610.12646v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the construction of unitary $t$-designs in a multi-photon Fock space on programmable linear-optical interferometers. Using the frame potential as the optimization objective, we identify architectures that realize approximate unitary 1- and 2-designs with considerably fewer controllable parameters than required for universal linear optics. For example, we find numerical evidence suggesting that for unitary 1-designs, the required number of programmable parameters scales empirically as $2d$ with the number of modes $d$, instead of $O(d^2)$. We benchmark the resulting ensembles using single-photon transition probabilities and average channel fidelities. Furthermore, as a practical result, we develop a photon-number estimation protocol for multi-photon Fock states that leverages these optimized 1- and 2-designs. Our findings demonstrate that shallow interferometers can accurately reproduce Haar-averaged first moments, while second-moment-sensitive observables provide a considerably stricter test for approximate unitary 2-designs.

items.title: Quantum Information-Theoretic Analysis of Optical Fiber Sensing via Stimulated Brillouin Scattering
items.summary: arXiv:2610.12980v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) is a powerful mechanism for distributed sensing in optical fibers, as the Brillouin response is highly sensitive to local material parameters. Assuming the input probe is a quantum state, we develop a quantum-information-theoretic framework for SBS-based fiber sensing and intrusion detection. Starting from a linearized opto-acoustic Hamiltonian, we derive an effective input-output relation for a short fiber segment. We then model each fiber segment as a single-mode bosonic Gaussian channel and the entire fiber as a cascade of quantum channels. We then compute the quantum Fisher information for general SBS-dependent parameters and identify optimal measurement settings to achieve the quantum limit, comparing them with receiver-constrained strategies such as heterodyne detection and photon counting. In addition, we propose an adaptive approach that achieves first-order asymptotic optimality and provides a novel second-order correction to address preliminary miscalibration. As an application, we apply the framework to the fiber-tapping detection problem.

items.title: All-optical deconvolution via quantum cross-correlation spectroscopy with bright twin beams
items.summary: arXiv:2610.13074v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The resolution of spectroscopic measurements is fundamentally limited by the convolution between a system's intrinsic response and the instrument response function, creating an ill-posed inverse problem. While entangled photons can theoretically bypass these limits, low photon flux has hindered their experimental realization. Here, we propose quantum cross-correlation spectroscopy (QCCS), utilizing macroscopic twin beams (signal and idler beams) to physically circumvent this convolution limit in coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering. Employing the signal beam as a broadband probe, QCCS achieves all-optical deconvolution through a correlation-enhanced sum-frequency generation channel between the convoluted anti-Stokes and idler beams. By subtracting the uncorrelated background using a 500-femtosecond temporal window, we successfully retrieve narrow Raman bands (8 cm^{-1} and 15 cm^{-1}) completely obscured by a 75 cm^{-1} probe bandwidth without numerical deconvolution or prior knowledge. Our results establish macroscopic quantum correlations as a robust resource for high-fidelity spectroscopy, paving the way for ultrashort-pulse-free operando studies under natural, incoherent excitation conditions.

items.title: Solitons in the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with the pseudo-Raman term, anti-diffusion gain and nonlinear loss
items.summary: arXiv:2610.13255v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a nonconservative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (NLSE) which includes additional nonlinear terms accounting for the pseudo-stimulated-Raman-scattering (pseudo-SRS) effect and cubic loss. An essentially novel feature of the model is the linear anti-diffusion gain, which leads to the obvious blow-up in the infinite or spatially periodic system. We consider the absorptive boundary conditions, which suppress the blow-up driven by effective convective instability in the setup. The NSLE model is derived, in the extended adiabatic approximation, from the underlying Zakharov system, which includes the viscosity term acting on its low-frequency component and the anti-diffusion gain in the high-frequency (HF) one. The latter term appears if the expansion, with respect to the deviation of the wavenumber, is performed not around the minimum-loss point (as in the usual situation), but around a maximum-loss point. Dynamics of moving solitons in the model is addressed by means of analytical and numerical methods. The sech approximation for the soliton predicts it as a stable fixed point (FP) of the system of balance equations for the HF norm and wave momentum, derived in the moving reference frame. The FP attraction basin is identified too. The predictions are corroborated by direct simulations of the full NSLE with the absorptive boundary conditions.

items.title: Judd-Ofelt analysis and coherent spectroscopy of europium-based molecular complexes for quantum information applications
items.summary: arXiv:2610.13664v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rare-earth-ion based molecular crystals are emerging as a promising platform for quantum information applications, combining long optical coherence times with the chemical tunability of coordination chemistry. Here we present a comprehensive optical characterisation of twelve Eu$^{3+}$-based molecular complexes, with a focus on the coherent $^{5}\text{D}_{0} \longrightarrow \ ^{7}\text{F}_{0}$ transition at $\sim$580 nm. Judd-Ofelt analyses are performed across all complexes, providing insights into ligand-field environments, local point-group symmetries, and the resulting branching ratios of the coherent transition. We find that lower point-group symmetry (C$_1$, C$_2$) yields higher branching ratios of the $^{5}\text{D}_{0} \longrightarrow \ ^{7}\text{F}_{0}$ transition, exceeding 1\% in several complexes. Optical inhomogeneous linewidths measured at 4.2 K reveal narrow linewidths for some complexes of below ten GHz, indicative of a highly ordered crystalline environment. Optical coherence measurements of one of the complexes, 5-Eu, yields an optical coherence time of $T_{\text{2}}^{\text{opt}} = 2.3~\mu\mathrm{s}$ at 4.2 K, comparable to the best-performing molecular systems reported to date. Systematic characterisation and quantitative comparison will be key to find structure-property relations guiding rational design of optimised complexes for quantum information applications.

items.summary: 此次发布的A3还是有些许不同，相比之前的公板方案和终端入库，自主品牌手机搭载绝对属于深度合作：一是首次选择非Adroid操作系统，是基于YunOS的手机；二是YunOS生态首次迎来运营商自主品牌的手机；三是对中移动和阿里巴巴在产业示范和引领都都具有双赢价值。

两会关注：提速降费步伐加快，三大运营商打出全新组合拳
items.summary: 年两会总理提出了2017年“网络提速降费要迈出更大步伐”，并明确了三个方向：年内全部取消手机国内长途和漫游费；大幅降低中小企业互联网专线接入资费；降低国际长途电话费。为了响应政府号召，三大运营商都公布了2017年提速降费的新政，通过一些列组合拳持续推进提速降费。

items.title: 大招齐发，英特尔直击网络转型
items.summary: 运营商是实现5G连接及应用和业务创新的重要基石，也是网络转型的主角。作为中国三大运营商之一的中国电信，正在努力推进网络转型，为5G的到来做好准备。中国电信选择与英特尔合作，采用英特尔RSD实施方案，联手击破运营商在网络转型中的各个难题，真正做到在网络转型之路所向披靡。

items.title: Juniper今年发力电信市场：重振国内运营商业务
items.summary: 日前，Juniper Networks (瞻博网络) 举办了主题为飞跃的合作伙伴大会。在会上，瞻博网络大中国区总裁林小平表示，今年Juniper将重点发力运营商、OTT、企业市场及BTI、Contrail业务。其中，运营商市场是Juniper第一要发展的市场。

items.title: 中国电信六大新举措持续推进提速降费
items.summary: 今天上午，国务院新闻办公室举办国务院政策吹风会。根据会议的内容显示，2017年10月1日起，三大运营商将全部取消手机国内长途和漫游费。此外，运营商还需要进一步提速降费。作为三大运营商之一的中国电信响应国家号召，2017年中国电信推出六大新举措，持续推进提速降费。

items.title: 超260个云项目背后：华为助力运营商建好云、用好云、管好云
items.summary: 作为产业界云化领域的创新中坚力量之一，以及对IT和通信皆有深刻洞察的解决方案提供者，华为IT产品线过去一年中持续在全球运营商数字化转型中发挥重要战略伙伴的作用，在市场上的表现亦是“超乎想象”，据披露已经与运营商合作展开了超过260个有关云的项目。

items.title: 北京移动创新产品服务体系：“司马大数据”今年营收有望过亿
items.summary: 杜洋介绍，2017年，司马大数据的目标是进一步扩大服务能力和市场规模，为更多的客户提供精准的大数据服务；同时向合作伙伴提供能力开放，促进行业内同仁发挥自身特长，百花齐放，开发和拓展大数据行业市场。具体规划主要体现在以下三方面：标准产品规模化；行业深耕，开发行业解决方案；能力开放。在营收方面，北京移动2017年大数据收入目标是1亿元。

items.title: 中国移动智能家庭网关设备集采：上海贝尔获得50%份额
items.summary: 备受关注的中国移动2017年智能家庭网关设备集中采购（公开部分模型二）已于日前结束。此次集采共有三家企业中标，上海贝尔获得50%份额，烽火获得30%，华为获得20%。

items.title: MWC 2017大连接雏形显现：产业链各方合作更紧密
items.summary: 在日前召开的2017世界移动大会上，物联网虽然被5G抢了风头，实际上依然成为参展企业重点展示的一大环节，更智能化的汽车、更智能的家居产品展示着实吸引了无数用户眼球。在千亿联接和万亿市场的巨大吸引之下，运营商、通信设备商、IT厂商、软件公司和互联网企业等各方势力，纷纷摩拳擦掌，竞逐这个潜力无穷的“风口”市场。

items.title: 对话英特尔：产业协作与标准化助推5G成功
items.summary: 5G不仅仅是为了手机而设计的，更多的是用于未来的智慧城市、智能家居以及VR等场景。在这个过程中，英特尔和产业合作伙伴也需要不断地学习，从测试当中不断地学习和调整技术和解决方案。英特尔扮演着独特的贡献的角色，通过前期测试当中不断吸取经验和教训，来反馈到标准化的制定当中，让更多的产业合作伙伴受益。

items.title: 工信部对我国网络强国建设提出四点建议
中兴许明解读有线五大亮点：大带宽有大机遇
items.summary: 在本届MWC中兴通讯展台，有线产品家族集体亮相，占据了展厅的重要位置。中兴通讯高级副总裁许明在展台上接受C114等媒体采访，解读了有线产品本次展出的五大亮点。

items.title: 徐直军详解视频驱动力与挑战：华为助力运营商淘金万亿级新市场
items.summary: 徐直军在2017世界移动大会期间的Keynote上发表了“让视频成为运营商增长的新动力”的主题演讲。他指出，内容、视频正在重新定义电信产业，对运营商来说视频业务已成必须，华为将自己定位为运营商视频业务成功的使能者，帮助运营商发展视频业务并获得增长。

items.title: 京东发布2016年财报:营收达2602亿元 同比增44%
items.summary: 京东发布2016年全年业绩核心数据。数据显示，2016年京东全年净收入为2602亿元人民币，同比增长44%，并实现年度扭亏为盈，非美国通用会计准则下（Non-GAAP）年度净利润达10亿元人民币。

items.title: 百度承认旗下hao123暗藏恶意代码：向用户道歉 已清除
items.summary: 今天上午百度旗下网站hao123针对前两天火绒安全实验室发布报告《百度旗下网站暗藏恶意代码 劫持用户电脑疯狂“收割”流量》，向用户进行道歉，并且声称已经清除恶意代码。

items.title: 联想业绩下滑7成 16亿再卖楼：确能提亮财报
items.summary: 3月2日，联想集团公告称，旗下全资附属公司联想（北京）有限公司已与北京融创融科地产有限公司订立了一份股权转让协议，将以约人民币16.17亿元的价格向后者出售成都联创融锦投资有限责任公司49%股权。公告透露，成都联创融锦及其子公司主要从事住宅和商业地产开发业务。

items.title: MWC 2017之无线篇：设备商5G竞赛正式打响
items.summary: 在近日于西班牙巴塞罗那举行2017世界移动大会(Mobile World Congress，MWC 2017)上，5G无疑是本次展会的最大亮点之一。在此期间，各5G研发组织、运营商、设备商、学术界以及合作伙伴等产业链各方在5G研发方面的最新进展备受业界关注。其中，移动通信设备商纷纷选择在大会期间发布重磅新品和解决方案，以期在5G竞赛中占得先机。

items.title: 英特尔助力电信网络转型 让5G不再是“看上去很美”
items.summary: 实现5G愿景，可并不仅仅是从基站到手机终端那点事。对无线技术进行革新，只是5G万里长征中的一段路。虽然对于普通消费者而言，这是他们未来能够从手机端看到的变革，但更多他们看不到的变化——电信运营商网络的转型。

items.title: 中国联通与德国电信携手发展物联网 建立战略合作伙伴关系
items.summary: 双方将共同致力于提高物联网连接能力，促进现有技术和窄带物联网等新技术发展以及物联网平台扩展，为共同抓住在欧洲和中国的商机、实现两家公司的持续增长奠定坚实基础。中国联通总经理陆益民和德国电信管理委员会成员克劳迪娅出席了签约仪式，双方就开展广泛深入的合作进行了交流。

items.title: 长光华芯上半年营收3.91亿元 同比增长82.67%
items.summary: 2026年上半年公司实现营业收入3.91亿元，同比上升 82.67%；归属于上市公司股东净利润 3,033.78 万元，同比增长238.04%；归属于上市公司的扣除非经常性损益的净利润-1,038.44万元。

items.title: 有方科技上半年营收同比减少42.04% 净利润同比增长17.36%
items.summary: 报告期内，上半年公司实现营业收入9.70亿元，同比减少42.04%；归属于上市公司股东的净利润7459.74万元，同比增长17.36%；扣除非经常性损益后的净利润7245.70万元，同比增长22.60%。基本每股收益0.81元。

items.title: 美格智能上半年净利润同比增长25.85% Q2单季营收破10亿元创历史新高
items.summary: C114讯 8月31日消息（颜翊）日前，美格智能发布2026年半年度报告。报告显示，公司上半年实现营业收入20.25亿元，同比增长7.32%；归属于上市公司股东的净利润1.06亿元，同比增长25.85%；扣非净利润1.07亿元，同比增长29.84%。

items.title: 广和通上半年营收37.78亿元增长1.92% 净利润同比下降71.63%
items.summary: 报告期内，公司实现营业收入37.78亿元，同比增长1.92%；实现归母净利润6182.43万元，同比下降71.63%。

items.title: 频准激光上半年营收2.56亿元增42.13% 净利润增24.58%
items.summary: C114讯 8月27日消息（颜翊）昨日，本月18日刚刚上市的量子科技公司频准激光披露首份半年度业绩报告，2026年上半年，公司实现营业收入2.56亿元，同比增长42.13%；实现归母净利润8833.57万元，同比增长24.58%。

items.title: 亨通光电上半年净利润31.2亿元 同比增长93.38%
items.summary: 亨通光电披露2026年半年度报告。报告期内，公司实现营业收入420.26亿元，同比增长31.13%； 实现归属于上市公司股东的净利润31.20亿元，同比增长93.38%；实现扣除非经常性损益的净利润31.51亿元，同比增长100.62%。

items.title: 华工科技：2026年上半年，光互联业务营收38.03亿元
items.summary: 华工科技2026年上半年营收78.22亿元，光互联业务达38.03亿元，AI高速光模块快速放量，实现1.6T至3.2T技术跨越及硅光芯片规模化应用。

items.title: 英伟达第二财季营收962.21亿美元 同比增长106%
items.summary: 颜翊）英伟达发布2027财年第二季度财报。本季营收 962.21 亿美元，同比增长 106%；净利润达到596.88亿美元，同比增长126%，毛利率75.0%（GAAP与非GAAP口径一致）。

items.title: 光互联测试产品需求激增，联讯仪器上半年净利润同比增长903%
items.summary: 联讯仪器2026年上半年净利润达5.67亿元，同比增903%；受益AI算力与光模块扩产，高速通信及CPO测试设备放量，毛利率升至70.79%，研发投入同比增长83.34%。

items.title: 中科曙光上半年净利9.71亿元 同比增长33.31%
items.summary: 昨日，中科曙光发布2026年半年度报告。报告期内，公司实现营业收入74.66亿元，同比增长27.62%；归属于上市公司股东的净利润9.71亿元，同比增长33.31%；扣非后净利润8.44亿元，同比大幅增长48.45%。

items.title: 通宇通讯上半年营收5.82亿元同比增长9.32% 海外收入占比超五成
items.summary: 通宇通讯昨日发布半年度报告。报告显示，2026年上半年，公司实现营业收入5.82亿元，同比增长9.32%；但归属于上市公司股东的净利润为-2233.12万元，较上年同期的2178.60万元由盈转亏，同比下降202.50%。

items.title: 海能达上半年实现营收22.62亿元 同比增长0.11%
items.summary: 海能达昨日公布了2026年半年度报告。报告期内，公司实现营收22.62亿元，同比增长0.11%；若剔除去年同期西班牙子公司并表影响，上半年营收同比增长11.79%；归属上市公司股东的净利润为4,260万元，同比下降 54.48%。

items.title: 新易盛上半年营收209.1亿元，同比增长100.34%
items.summary: 新易盛2026年上半年营收209.1亿元，同比增100.34%；光模块产品覆盖400G-12.8T，布局硅光、TFLN、CPO等前沿技术。

items.title: 铭普光磁上半年光通信业务同比增长5%
items.summary: 铭普光磁日前发布了2026年半年度报告。报告显示，上半年营收10.63亿元，同比增长31.88%；净利润-1539万元，去年同期-7304万元。扣非后净利润-2353万元，去年同期-7779万元。

items.title: 长飞上半年净利润29.25亿元，同比增长888.88%
items.summary: 长飞公司日前发布了2026年半年度报告。报告显示，长飞上半年实现营收98.09亿元，同比大增53.64%；净利润29.25亿元，同比增长888.88%。扣非后净利润24.49亿元，同比增长1680.48%。

items.title: 东山精密上半年光模块业务收入53.51亿元，占营收比19.25%
items.summary: 东山精密2026年上半年光模块业务收入53.51亿元，依托索尔思实现EML光芯片IDM量产，并推进1.6T/3.2T光模块及硅光技术布局。

items.title: 中际旭创上半年营收417.78亿元，同比增长182.49%
items.summary: 中际旭创2026年上半年营收417.78亿元，同比增182.49%，受益于AI驱动的高速光模块（800G/1.6T）放量及海外收入占比近95%。

items.title: 构建开源开放人才生态，夯实产业自主根基｜2026华为ICT学院年会圆满举办
items.summary: 华为全联接大会期间，2026华为ICT学院年会同期举办。本次年会汇聚教育行业组织、全国高校代表、产业生态伙伴及行业技术专家，紧扣AI时代产业变革与高等教育改革双重需求，聚焦CANN算力生态建设、硬核技术创新、拔尖人才培育三大核心方向，探索产教深度融合新路径，打通产业技术迭代与高校人才培养衔接壁垒，为我国计算产业自主可控、高质量发展筑牢人才底座。

items.title: 华为全联接大会2026全光峰会举办，F5G-A全光网加速AI普惠千行万业
items.summary: 华为全联接大会2026期间，以“光智共融，F5G-A全光网加速AI普惠千行万业”为主题的华为全光峰会成功举办。来自全球的500余位行业专家、客户及合作伙伴齐聚一堂，深入探讨“光智共融”驱动行业升级的新路径与创新实践。

items.title: 全国首个！内蒙古移动携手华为完成露天矿山场景5G-A千兆上行验证
items.summary: 近日，中国移动内蒙古公司（简称“内蒙古移动”）联合华为技术有限公司（简称“华为”）在呼伦贝尔华能伊敏露天矿，顺利完成全国首个露天矿山场景5G-A千兆上行网络能力验证。依托 4.9GHz+F/A SUL 辅助上行技术，现场实测单用户上行峰值速率达到 1022Mbps，标志内蒙古自治区正式迈入5G-A“千兆上行”新时代，为区域数字经济高质量发展注入新动能。

items.title: 华为梁策：迈向全面智能化，拥抱AI新时代
items.summary: 华为提出“以网为基、以智为翼”战略，助力运营商构建算力底座、升级新一代通信网，并通过AItoX赋能个人、家庭、行业市场，推动Token经营等创新模式落地。

items.title: 光智共融，加速AI园区建设：华为携手产业各方共探F5G-A全光园区新实践

items.title: 山东大学携手华为发布校园L4自智网络联合创新成果，重构高校教育数智化底座

Engineering Multipole Resonances in Dielectric Metasurfaces for Transmission, Reflection, and Absorption Control
items.summary: Dielectric metasurfaces have moved to the forefront of nanophotonics, offering flat, low-loss alternatives to conventional bulk optical elements for controlling the amplitude, phase, and polarization of light. These structures are of growing interest to researchers and engineers working on sensing, energy harvesting, and flat optics, as their performance hinges on precisely engineered optical resonances. Full-wave finite element simulation, combined with semianalytical multipole decomposition in the COMSOL Multiphysics® software, gives us a way to not only predict these resonances but also uncover their underlying physical origins. In this webinar, Dr. Pavel Terekhov, postdoctoral researcher at National Institute of Standards and Technology, will trace how a single quadrumer meta-atom, originally studied for its magnetic octupole response, evolves into two distinct light manipulation regimes. He will first revisit the foundational single-particle results that motivated this work, then show how arranging quadrumers into a periodic crystalline silicon metasurface produces anomalous absorption enhancement, governed by two independent multipole mechanisms coexisting in the same structure. Building on this, he will then introduce ongoing work on a gallium nitride metasurface, where the complex interplay of four different multipoles is used to sculpt reflection and transmission spectra including the quasi-bound-states-in-the-continuum (q-BIC) manipulation. Attendees will see how COMSOL Multiphysics® and multipole decomposition connect full-wave simulation and analytical insight, turning abstract resonance behavior into physically interpretable design rules. The broader takeaway is that multipole-based simulation is not just a diagnostic tool but a design strategy: It enables the on-demand tailoring of absorption, reflection, and transmission in dielectric metasurfaces, with direct relevance to sensing, energy harvesting, and future optical device applications. items.title: Hybrid quantum computers could finally get to grips with light and matter
items.summary: Many of nature's most important processes depend on how particles of matter interact with light and other force-carrying particles. So far, however, it has proven difficult for conventional computers to determine how individual particles behave in these interactions.

items.title: Quantum 'birthmarks' hold lasting traces of a system's past
items.summary: Some classical physical systems can explore many configurations over time until their long-term behavior no longer reveals their starting conditions. The sampling of available configurations according to the appropriate statistical distribution is a property called ergodicity.

items.title: Ultraviolet laser pulses engineer diamond defects selectively, leaving quantum qubits intact
items.summary: When we think about a diamond, we often think about a material whose value comes from its perfection. In my research, however, I am interested in something almost opposite: the tiny imperfections inside diamonds. These atomic-scale defects can give diamonds new optical and electronic properties, and some of them can serve as quantum systems. The challenge is learning how to control these defects without disturbing the others.

items.title: New stability rules distinguish quantum phases of matter that an older method wrongly groups together
items.summary: Most of us recognize basic phases of matter and their properties: solids maintain their shape, liquids flow freely with constant volume, and gases expand to fill their container. Quantum phases, on the other hand, are much harder to categorize, overturning traditional notions of what a phase even is and forcing physicists to rethink their definitions.

items.title: Hybrid quantum computer observes foundational quantum effect in a new setting
items.summary: Physicists in the Department of Physics at the University of Oxford have used a hybrid quantum computer, made up of qubits and quantum oscillators, to observe the Aharonov–Bohm effect in a quantum simulation. The effect is a quantum phenomenon in which a particle can acquire a measurable phase by traveling around a magnetic flux, even though it never passes through a region where a magnetic field is present.

items.title: Three quantum-inspired cores leave opposite fingerprints on the ringing of black holes
items.summary: Every black hole hides a question at its center. Einstein's theory predicts that whatever falls in is crushed into a singularity, a point of infinite density where the theory itself breaks down. Most physicists expect quantum gravity to replace that point with something finite. But the center lies hidden behind the horizon. How could we ever learn what is there?

items.title: Quantum chip holds multiple photons at once, opening path to scalable memory
items.summary: For highly fragile quantum information systems, the ability to store quantum information is vital—but also challenging. Quantum information is transported in particles of light called photons, which often must be temporarily paused (or "stored") while other, slower quantum operations catch up. This storage must be performed on microchips as small as 1 centimeter (0.4 inches)—a distance covered by light in a few trillionths of a second. Storing photons for a microsecond would represent a massive leap forward for the capabilities of quantum chips.

items.title: Light reads electron spins inside porous crystals, opening path to quantum chemical sensors
items.summary: University of Glasgow researchers are part of an international collaboration that could lead to a new generation of quantum sensors. The team, which included researchers from the University of Tokyo, University of Glasgow, University of Sheffield and Kobe University, has for the first time used light to read out the magnetic spin of electrons trapped inside a porous crystalline material known as a metal-organic framework (MOF).

items.title: Ultrafast core-level spectroscopy reveals elusive precursors of exciton condensation in quantum materials
items.summary: Many fascinating phases in quantum materials emerge when electrons, atoms and other microscopic components begin to act collectively. But these phases do not necessarily appear out of nowhere when a material crosses a transition temperature. Before long-range order develops, microscopic fluctuations can already be present.

items.title: Lensless imaging method enables long-term monitoring of living cells without staining
items.summary: In a study led by Tampere University, researchers have developed a new lensless imaging method that produces precise quantitative data on living cells from a single image. The compact system can be placed inside a standard cell-culture incubator, allowing living cells to be monitored continuously for hours or even days without staining or other labels. The research is published in the journal Applied Physics Letters.

items.title: How researchers tell different quantum excitations apart in individual molecules
items.summary: Molecules can be placed in a wide variety of quantum states. How can these states be distinguished in measurements when theoretical models are unreliable? Which excitation process lies behind which measurement signal?

items.title: Layered semiconductor unlocks magnetic control of light emitted by quantum condensates
items.summary: Quantum technologies are considered key technologies of the future. However, research in this field requires not only scientific expertise but sometimes also highly specialized laboratory conditions. Bose–Einstein condensates are a remarkable example, in which atoms move in lockstep, making quantum-mechanical effects visible not only at the level of individual atoms but also on a macroscopic scale. The first Bose–Einstein condensates were observed in ultracold atomic gases at temperatures close to absolute zero. The cooling required to achieve this was technically demanding, costly and restricted to specialized laboratories.

items.title: Gravity and light reveal how liquids turn into thin fibers
items.summary: From spiders spinning their webs to the manufacturing of textiles, the formation of fibers from liquids plays an important role in both nature and industry. Yet accurately predicting the properties of such fibers remains a challenge. The fiber is often much thinner than the nozzle from which a polymer or solution is extruded. Factors such as temperature, flow conditions and chemical reactions ultimately determine a fiber's thickness and strength.

items.title: Ultrashort laser pulses let new microscope map electron interactions across thin materials
items.summary: A new type of advanced microscope (wide-field coherent multidimensional microscopy) has been developed. It uses a carefully designed sequence of ultrashort light pulses to study the behavior of high-tech materials, with potential practical applications in the study of innovative materials such as those used to build solar panels. This is the result of work by a research group of physicists from the Faculty of Sciences, Mathematics, Physics, and Natural Sciences at Università Cattolica's Brescia campus who, for the first time, have developed a "multidimensional microscope" that, in a sense, records the behavior of materials.

items.title: First observation of quantum spins shifting a centimeter-scale object in the lab
items.summary: Modern technological breakthroughs like lasers, MRI scanners, semiconductors and quantum computers rest on the study of quantum mechanics. However, the field has predominantly focused on (sub)atomic phenomena far removed from our human senses.

items.title: Levitating glass sphere becomes entangled with light at room temperature
items.summary: Today, many physicists are actively exploring how light could be used to link objects through quantum entanglement. By fully harnessing the effect, they hope to unlock a wide array of applications, from secure communication networks spanning vast distances to sensitive new tests of the fundamental laws of physics.

items.title: Quantum computing shortcut makes particle collisions easier to simulate
items.summary: Collisions between particles at high energies can sometimes produce new particles and shed light on interactions between the fundamental constituents of matter. Simulating these collisions and their underlying processes could yield valuable insights into how matter behaves at extremely small scales.
